Lately I've been nostalgic for bodybuilding style training.

I've been trying to lay out a calisthenics bodybuilding program in my head, but I realized I hadn't seen a thread for that here.

I know from prior conversations here that a lot of you focus on bodybuilding in your workouts. I was thinking we could stockpile our explicitly bodybuilding focused info somewhere.

My current plan is a 6 day split:

Chest: dips, decline pushups

Back: Pull ups, inverted shrugs

Legs: Horse stance etc. plus "cherry pickers" for hamstrings

Shoulders: Handstand pushups

Arms: Diamond push ups, underhand grip inverted rows, grip/forearm work

Core: front & side plank

Each workout I plan to just hammer each indicated thing with tons of volume, usually in sets of 10. As you guys know by now I'm a volume nut, so emphasis is on total work volume. Might include some rep tempo stuff.

I've never trained exclusively for aesthetics, but as a tall, skinny fuck I have to do some hypertrophy specific work so I'm not some kind of weak skeleton man. So when I was running Starting Strength I threw in bicep curls, rows, and shrugs much earlier than the routine suggested. As for bodyweight stuff:

I encountered this bodyweight version of Arnold's famous Golden Six program. I made a number of changes, such as:

  1. Adding Rows and some kind of hip-hinge movement. I would throw the rows in right after the close-grip chin-ups and the hip-hinge movement in at the end of the cycle. Helps to balance out ratio of pushing and pulling movement in the routine.

  2. Changing pistol squats to something more effective, like weighted Cossack Squats. Almost anything is a better mass builder than pistol squats.

  3. Substitute pull-ups for Gironda Pull-ups.

  4. Substitute Hanging Leg Raises for sit-ups.

I like to add handstand work for my traps, I find that shifting my weight to one side, raising the opposite hand, putting it on my chest for 1 second, while shrugging my shoulders. I've heard one source call this a "Handstand Kong" but I've never seen that anywhere else. It was in the Boxer's Book of Conditioning and Drilling by Mark Hatmaker, if you're wondering.

For my calves, I go on long-ass walks. I could do hundreds of calf-raises, but I prefer hiking.

I target my neck with Wrestler's Bridges and Front Bridges. It's possibly the only case where it's possible to gain too much mass in surprisingly little time, so I do that once a week.

For forearms, I use towels draped over the chin-up bar, paired with fingertip push-ups to hit my grip muscles. Farmers walks are great, especially with sandbags or sacks of dog food.

And of course, I use some of the rest-pause techniques from that article in the sidebar. Seriously, it's pure gold for training bodyweight bodybuilding.
